title: Function signature fingerprint watchdog and semantic-diff canary policy
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Objective: Add a lightweight, deterministic fingerprinting layer for function-call signatures and a semantic-diff scoring policy that runs as part of canary, A/B, and shadow rollouts. The goal is to detect subtle incompatible changes to structured outputs (function name, argument names/types, nested schemas) and surface a single scalar score to driving rollout decisions and automated rollback.

Background: We frequently see function-call surface regressions that are syntactically small (renamed fields, reordered args, optional->required flips) but cause downstream consumer breakage. Existing schema validators are brittle to non-breaking reorders and do not capture semantic differences (e.g., argument renamed from "dest" to "destination" but equivalent). The team needs a middle-ground: a deterministic fingerprint + semantic-diff heuristic we can compute at scale in shadow and canary flows without executing downstream systems.

Proposed design:
1) Canonicalization pipeline: normalize function signatures and outputs before hashing. Steps: lowercase names, remove punctuation, sort named arguments by canonical key, collapse aliases (via a small alias map), and normalize primitive type synonyms (int->integer). For nested objects apply key-order independent serialization.
2) Fingerprint: compute a 64-bit hash (xxhash64) of the canonicalized signature plus a compact shape summary (field counts, nest depth). Store fingerprint along with an entropy slab (small vector of 3 integer buckets) used for coarse grouping in telemetry.
3) Semantic-diff scorer: on top of raw fingerprint equality, compute a weighted diff between canonicalized ASTs of the signature and an existing baseline. Heuristics include: name edit-distance, type-change penalty, arity delta, optional->required penalty, new required fields penalty, removed fields penalty, and nested-structure distance. Combine heuristics into a 0..100 score (0 = identical, 100 = high-risk incompatible).
4) Canary policy: treat fingerprint equality as pass. If fingerprint differs, evaluate semantic-diff score. Policy thresholds: score <= 10 -> auto pass (low risk), 10 < score <= 30 -> soft-block (require PM/owner approval to advance), score > 30 -> hard-block and trigger immediate diversion of traffic and rollback if observed in production beyond warmup window.
5) Shadow probing: all candidate model variants run through a shadow probe that records both fingerprint and semantic features. Probes run in a sandboxed runner that executes function-call plumbing but drops side effects. We attach lightweight checksum of serialized outputs to minimize storage.
6) Rollout integration: integrate with rollout orchestrator so that the policy influences ramp rates. We expose a single numeric compatibility metric on the rollout dashboard and allow automated abort rules when metric exceeds thresholds or when downstream consumer error rates increase concurrently.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fingerprint generation is deterministic across server restarts and language SDKs (implement canonicalizer in Go + typescript libs).
- Semantic-diff score computed for 95% of function-call variants within 50ms p95 in the probe path.
- New scoreboard visible in Console per-rollout with histogram of scores and top-5 contributing differences.
- Playbook enacted: any deployment with score>30 at >1% traffic for 10 minutes -> automatic pause + alert to oncall + optional auto-rollback.

Telemetry and metrics to capture:
- fingerprint_match_rate per rollout
- semantic_diff_score distribution
- percent_of_deployments_unblocked_by_approval
- false_positive_rate estimated by sampling known-compatible changes

Rollout schedule:
- Phase 0: landing PR and spec (this ticket) -> implementation spike (2d)
- Phase 1: canonicalizer + hash library + unit tests (3d)
- Phase 2: probe runner integration + telemetry (3d)
- Phase 3: dashboard and playbook wiring + PM signoff (2d)
- Phase 4: gradually enable on internal canaries, then public canaries at 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 48 hours with manual hold points.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for canonicalizer edge cases (aliases, nested reorderings, optional fields).
- Fuzz corpus derived from existing function-call traffic to validate that known-safe transformations keep score <= 10.
- Integration test that simulates A/B traffic with a variant that renames one argument and asserts score falls in expected band.

Dependencies:
- rollout-operator (ENG-110827) for API hooks
- console-telemetry schema update (PM-330)
- typescript SDK canonicalizer (DX-98)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: semantic heuristic tuning may be noisy and cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds, enable soft-block for mid scores and require human approval. Collect labeled examples to refine ML-based scoring later.
- Risk: perf regression in probe path. Mitigation: keep canonicalizer optimized and run profiling; fall back to fingerprint-only path if probe p95 exceeds target.

Open questions:
- Should we include example payload signatures (sample output tokens) in the diff to capture semantic changes not visible in schema? (privacy/size trade-off).
- Ownership: small alias map needs a config UI for product teams to register intended renames. Where does that live?

Deliverables: canonicalizer library (go/js), probe integration, rollout operator checks, Console scoreboard, playbook with rollback automation, and a short confluence runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic fingerprinting implemented and library published in Go and TypeScript
Semantic-diff scoring returns values within 0..100 and is computed p95<=50ms in probe path
Rollout orchestration honors the policy thresholds and can auto-pause or rollback per playbook
Console shows per-rollout compatibility distribution and top contributors to score
